96→
97→The native shader-canvas UI lane now follows this contract:

122→UI reload and derived-value semantics now follow an explicit compiler-to-runtime contract:

125→- `kain-ui` owns runtime execution of those contracts, including derived recompute, exact invalidation, hot-reload state transfer, reload patch reporting, and bounded reconciliation

132→### Native Packaging And Operator Loop
133→
134→The native packaging lane is the operator-facing loop for UI iteration:

136→- `kain-driver` materializes native apps as a package set, writing the runtime bundle, runtime contract, realtime bundle, `app_manifest.json`, `runtime_snapshot.json`, and any required sidecars into the app artifact tree.
137→- Generated launchers resolve those packaged sidecars beside the executable so the app boots from authored bundle truth instead of a debug-host template.
138→- The runtime snapshot is the reload/control surface, not hidden launcher state. It carries explicit provider, session, workspace, command, and capability records, including the `runtime.reload` command already emitted by the packaging path.
139→- Devtools and inspectors must stay opt-in and remain represented in packaged truth, not injected as default product chrome.
140→- When a packaged launch stops reflecting a change, check the materialized manifest and snapshot sidecars first. That is the stable operator boundary before assuming the host itself is wrong.

184→## Architectural Guardrails
185→
186→- Do not split semantic truth across runtime lanes.
187→- Do not let hosts re-parse source as the normal execution path.
188→- Do not invent lane-specific shader, UI, or compute metadata when compiler-owned bundles already exist.
189→- Prefer data-driven capabilities, manifests, registries, and bundle metadata over scattered string checks and host-local assumptions.
190→- Preserve the distinction between authored language semantics, importer behavior, and backend/runtime support.
191→- Platform- or console-specific render-command experiments should start as isolated adapter lanes under `smoketest/` or another dedicated adapter crate before any shared `kain-3D` contract is widened. The new `smoketest/3D/sm64_fast3d_smoke` is the pattern: it owns its own manifest, segment registry, display-list interpreter, and combiner logic instead of baking N64-specific assumptions into the common scene/material API too early.
192→- The SM64 import refresh workflow for that lane is now profile-driven and lives beside the smoke under `smoketest/3D/sm64_fast3d_smoke`. Use `refresh_sm64_import.bat` and `sm64_import_profile.render_us.json` instead of reconstructing long one-off `import-c` commands from memory.
193→- The same smoke now has a title-face extraction lane. `extract_sm64_title_face.bat`, `launch_title_face_visual_exe.bat`, and `capture_title_face_snapshot.bat` are the quickest path to a compiled proof that uses real extracted Mario face geometry while keeping N64-specific semantics inside the adapter.
194→- The adapter is no longer only a smoke-local runtime. The reusable host surface now lives in `crates/kain-fast3d-runtime`, while the smoke folder acts as a consumer that provides manifests, scripts, and validation assets.
195→- Keep the Fast3D lane data-driven. Its host startup now flows through crate-owned config files and env hooks (`KAIN_FAST3D_CONFIG`, `KAIN_FAST3D_MANIFEST`, `KAIN_FAST3D_SM64_ROOT`) rather than widening Kain language semantics or shared runtime contracts for one experimental console adapter.
196→- Native app launcher materialization now also supports generic host-sidecar packaging in `kain-driver`: generated launchers can copy arbitrary sidecars into the artifact/executable set, optionally export them as env vars, and switch between the default `run_bundled_app_json(...)` launcher path and a crate-owned no-arg entrypoint like `kain-fast3d-runtime::run_fast3d_cli()`. Preserve that mechanism as a generic host adapter capability, not a Fast3D-specific special case.
